But first you have to apply. Here's how to put your best foot forward. Understand the PIC and Why You Should Apply The

Understand the PIC and Why You Should Apply The President's Innovation Challenge is months-long startup competition designed to support student innovators across all 13 Harvard schools in turning their ideas into impact.
Applying to the PIC is more than just a chance to win significant financial support (up to $75,000 in non-dilutive funding for your venture).

Student applicants are divided among three student tracks: Health Care + Life Sciences Track: Open to any student-led venture in digital health/health IT, medical devices, diagnostics, therapeutics, biotech, and health care delivery.
Select the Health Care and Life Sciences track if clinical validation, regulatory pathway, reimbursement, or scientific risk shapes how you build and sell.
Non-medical ventures (such as health education, wellness, lifestyle, or patient community initiatives) belong in the Open Track.
Open Track: Open to student-led B2B and B2C ventures that prioritize revenue potential.
B2B ventures are selling to businesses, governments, schools, or other organizations.
This includes deep tech and climate tech ventures with intellectual property that may require additional scientific and technical validation.
B2C ventures are selling directly to individuals or through retail channels.
Social Impact Track: Open to student ventures that define success through measurable societal impact and a clear path to scale.
In addition to the judging process, all five finalists in each track will present a one-minute pitch on stage at the award ceremony.
The 2027 award ceremony is on May 5, 2027.

Browse all SIFF recipients Resources for SIFF applicants Social impact news + stories Subscribe to social innovation newsletter About the Fellowship Expand All Program Overview The Navab Social Impact Fellowship Fund was first established in 2019 through the generosity of Alexander Navab (MBA 1991) and then endowed by his widow Mary Kathryn Navab in 2025.
It is the Navab family’s hope that support from this fund helps recipients accelerate and advance their venture creation in social impact sectors.
SIFF awards $200,000 in grants annually, over the course of three pitch days (fall, spring, and summer with $60-75K distributed per semester).
Grants average between $4,000-15,000, though it can vary.
The Social Impact Fellowship Fund Committee reviews and evaluates all applications.
After the virtual pitch day, the SIFF judges determine the number of grants and grant amounts and notify winners.
The Fine Print By submitting an application, you consent to the release of information contained in your application to the Navab Social Impact Fellowship Fund.

Expand All Eligible Alumni + Affiliate Ventures Alumni and affiliate-led ventures currently participating in Launch Lab X , the Climate Circle , Pagliuca Harvard Life Lab , or Blavatnik Harvard Life Lab Longwood are eligible to compete in the PIC and will be placed in the appropriate alumni and affiliate track as semifinalists.

General Qualifications We encourage scalable ventures across all industries to apply, whether selling to businesses (B2B), selling to consumers (B2C), focusing on social impact or climate, or innovating in health care and life sciences.
Ventures that qualify as semifinalists typically have made substantive progress beyond the initial ideation and validation stages.
High-impact biotech, life sciences, or tough tech ventures that have done substantial technology validation and initial commercialization explorations are also encouraged to apply.
Early-stage ventures that are still validating customers and ideas are also encouraged to apply — especially those with innovative approaches to solving real-world problems.
If selected as a finalist, the venture's Harvard founder must pitch in person at the awards ceremony on May 5, 2027.

Terms of Use Competition Tracks Expand All Health Care + Life Sciences Track (Alumni + Affiliates) The Alumni + Affiliates Health Care + Life Sciences Track is open to ventures in Launch Lab X , the Climate Circle , the Blavatnik Harvard Life Lab Longwood , or the Pagliuca Harvard Life Lab that are improving the efficacy of health care services, including therapeutics, devices, and digital health.
Ventures may address a wide range of issues, from improving access to personalizing therapeutics.

Health Care + Life Sciences Track (Students) The Student Health Care + Life Sciences Track is open to any student-led venture in digital health/health IT, medical devices, diagnostics, therapeutics, biotech, and health care delivery.
Select the Health Care and Life Sciences track if clinical validation, regulatory pathway, reimbursement, or scientific risk shapes how you build and sell.
Non-medical ventures (such as health education, wellness, lifestyle, or patient community initiatives) belong in the Open Track.

Open Track (Alumni + Affiliates) The Alumni + Affiliates Open Track is open to ventures in Launch Lab X , the Climate Circle , the Blavatnik Harvard Life Lab Longwood , or the Pagliuca Harvard Life Lab .

The Climate Circle is open to both for-profit and nonprofit ventures with committed founders, clear traction, and growing momentum.
Climate Circle ventures span the globe: from Indonesia to Uganda, South Africa to the Midwestern U.S., Austria to Boston.
To be accepted into the Climate Circle, ventures must have moved beyond the idea stage.
